title: Children and older people as a share of the population
subtitle: Percentage of the population aged under 15 and aged 65 and over, 1950 to 2026.
key_fact: People aged 65 and over made up 16.1% of the population in 2026, compared with 10.7% in 1950.

title: Births, deaths and migration
subtitle: People born, people who died, and net migration (people arriving minus people leaving) in the twelve months to April, 1987 to 2026.
key_fact: In the twelve months to April 2026 there were 54,300 births and 35,400 deaths, and net migration added 48,100 people.

title: County populations since 1841
subtitle: Population of each county at each census from 1841 to 2022, as a percentage of its 1841 population. Use the slider to move through the census years.
key_fact: At the 2022 census, 21 of the 26 counties had fewer people than in 1841.

title: Population of Ireland
subtitle: Estimated number of people living in the State each April, 1950 to 2026.
key_fact: An estimated 5.53 million people lived in the State in April 2026, up 17% on 2016.

title: New homes completed each year
subtitle: Number of new dwellings completed in Ireland, 2012 to 2025.
key_fact: 36,215 new homes were completed in 2025, compared with 30,124 in 2024.

title: House prices
subtitle: Residential Property Price Index, January 2005 to August 2026. 100 is the average price level in 2015.
key_fact: In August 2026, house prices nationally were 110% above their 2015 average, before adjusting for inflation.

title: Average rent by county
subtitle: Average monthly rent on new private tenancies registered with the Residential Tenancies Board, 2008 to 2025. Use the slider to move through the years.
key_fact: In 2025, the average monthly rent on a new tenancy ranged from €977 in Donegal to €2,159 in Dublin.

title: Inflation
subtitle: Change in consumer prices compared with the same month a year earlier, November 1996 to October 2026.
key_fact: Consumer prices were 4.3% higher in October 2026 than a year earlier.

title: Price changes by type of spending
subtitle: Change in consumer prices for each main group of goods and services, October 2021 to October 2026.
key_fact: Over the five years to October 2026, prices rose most for housing and energy (+53.2%), compared with +24.0% for all items.

title: Average weekly earnings
subtitle: Average weekly earnings of employees, in cash terms and adjusted for consumer prices (in 2026 Q2 prices), 2008 Q1 to 2026 Q2.

sources.title: Average Earnings, Hours Worked, Employment and Labour Costs (EHQ03)

key_fact: Average weekly earnings were €1,047 in 2026 Q2, 3.9% higher than a year earlier, or 0.3% higher after adjusting for prices.

title: GDP and modified gross national income
subtitle: Gross domestic product (GDP) and modified gross national income (GNI*) in billions of euro at current prices, 1995 to 2025.

sources.title: Modified Gross National Income at Current Market Prices (NA001)

key_fact: In 2025, GNI* was €334 billion, 55% of GDP.

title: Unemployment rate
subtitle: Percentage of people in the labour force who are unemployed, seasonally adjusted, January 1998 to October 2026.
key_fact: The unemployment rate was 4.8% in October 2026, seasonally adjusted.

title: Recorded thefts and burglaries
subtitle: Number of theft and burglary incidents recorded by An Garda Síochána each year, by type, 2003 to 2025.
key_fact: 34,312 thefts from shops were recorded in 2025, compared with 15,692 in 2003.

title: Where people came from and went to
subtitle: Estimated number of immigrants by the country or region they came from, and emigrants by where they went, in the twelve months to April 2026.
key_fact: In the twelve months to April 2026, the largest group of emigrants, 14,600 people, went to the other countries that were EU members before 2004.

title: People moving to and from Ireland
subtitle: Estimated number of people who moved to Ireland (immigrants) and who left (emigrants) in the twelve months to April, 1987 to 2026.
key_fact: In the twelve months to April 2026, an estimated 110,600 people moved to Ireland and 62,500 left. Emigration was highest in 2012, at 83,000.

title: Deaths from heart disease, cancer and tuberculosis
subtitle: Deaths per 100,000 people each year from heart disease, cancer and tuberculosis, 1922 to 2023.
key_fact: The death rate from tuberculosis fell from 153 per 100,000 people in 1922 to 0.3 in 2023. Cancer has caused more deaths than heart disease in every year since 2003.

title: Life expectancy in Ireland and the EU
subtitle: Life expectancy at birth in years, Ireland and the 27 EU countries, 2018 to 2024.
key_fact: Life expectancy at birth in Ireland was 83.1 years in 2024, compared with an EU average of 81.5 years.

title: Greenhouse gas emissions by sector
subtitle: Ireland's greenhouse gas emissions in millions of tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, by sector, 1990 to 2024.
key_fact: Ireland's greenhouse gas emissions were 53.8 million tonnes in 2024, down from a peak of 70.8 million tonnes in 2001. Agriculture was the largest source, at 38% of the total.

title: Emissions per person in Ireland and the EU
subtitle: Greenhouse gas emissions per person in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, Ireland and the 27 EU countries, 2008 to 2024.
key_fact: In 2024, emissions were 10.0 tonnes per person in Ireland, compared with an EU average of 6.7 tonnes.

title: How often Irish speakers speak Irish
subtitle: People aged 3 and over who said they could speak Irish, by how often they speak it, Census 2022.

sources.title: Irish speakers aged 3 years and over (F8001)

key_fact: At the 2022 census, 1,873,997 people said they could speak Irish, and 71,968 (4% of them) said they spoke it every day outside school.

title: Daily Irish speakers in the Gaeltacht
subtitle: Percentage of people aged 3 and over in each Gaeltacht area who speak Irish every day outside school, Census 2011, 2016 and 2022.

sources.title: Daily Irish speakers aged 3 years and over (F8033)

key_fact: In 2022, 31% of people in the Gaeltacht spoke Irish every day outside school, compared with 35% in 2011.
